speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient being evaluated for systemic hypertension. To begin, how old are you and have you noticed any symptoms like headaches, vision changes, or fatigue recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Since this is a well-child visit in a 5-year-old with no medication use or family history of heart disease, let's proceed with the examination. Please describe your son's blood pressure readings from today's visit and whether the nurse noted any signs of fluid retention or abnormal pulse.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The finding of significantly elevated blood pressure in the right upper extremity, in the absence of hypertension in the lower extremities (which we assume is normal given the context), is the classic presentation for a coarctation of the aorta. This condition causes obstruction to blood flow, resulting in high pressure proximal to the narrowing (arms) and low pressure distal to it (legs).
